_readme: Every word the conversation panel says on its own, before the AI says anything. Edit the strings, reload, done — no code. What the AI itself knows about Elliot is NOT here: that is server/persona.ts, which is the only file the model ever reads, and it is kept off the client on purpose. 'questions' are the chips, in order. Only a few are on screen at a time (chat.ts decides how many); when one is asked it leaves and the next in this list takes its place, so the list can be long without the panel being a menu. Each one is sent to the AI verbatim as if the visitor had typed it, so they read as questions a person would actually ask, in the second person. 'fallback' is what Elliot says when the AI cannot be reached, by cause; none of those lines are generated either. 'live' labels the short lines under the header that are read live from his own accounts as the panel opens — Spotify, GitHub, Strava, WHOOP, Calendly — each one naming its source in small type and absent when there is nothing to show. 'more'/'less' is the toggle on the Spotify line that opens the last few tracks and the month's top artists.
questions: What did you actually do at Cassidy?
What are you looking for next?
What’s a weakness you’re working on?
What do you do outside of work?
What are you listening to right now?

fallback.unconfigured: I’ve lost my voice — the AI behind me isn’t switched on right now. The real Elliot is one email away: elliotgreenbaum@gmail.com.
fallback.busy: Give me a moment — too many questions at once. Try that one again in a minute.
fallback.error: Something went wrong on my end. Ask again, or email the real Elliot at elliotgreenbaum@gmail.com.
